description_en: Bhirat Darbāra Temple 2 is part of a complex that also includes two stone monuments surrounded by a stone wall. The site is located on top of a mountain directly to the west of the Gotijyula village, at an elevation of 2390 meters (7841 ft.). The summit of the massif is crowned by a vast open grassy area used for religious festivals and picnics. The entire area is thought to be the site of the Durbar of a king named Bhirat, or Birat. The historical identity of this character could not be determined at this time. Nonetheless, it is important to note that no architectural remnants have been discovered on the area's surface. The two structures are located at the northern end of the summit. A steep cliff lies directly north of them.The Temple 2 is a half-buried square structure. It has a single room that is buried 90 cm below ground level. No flight of steps or access to the floor could be located. A pillar measuring 110 x 95 cm and 151 cm in height stands in the centre of the room. Each side of the pillar has two small niches. The pillar and the walls that rest against the soil are made of roughly cut stone and constructed using dry masonry. The floor of the room is paved with long, slender, roughly cut slabs. The photographs taken some twenty years ago by French-Swiss archaeologist D. Baudais, show that the slabs were used as a kind of roofing for the room. They were placed resting on the soil edge on one side, and on the central pillar on the other side.North of this monument is a recently rebuilt square room with a central door on each side (JUM0480). It is also constructed of local stones and dry masonry. The exact purpose and origin of these two structures, known locally as temples, are unknown at this time. None of the existing material found in-situ appears to have been carved more than 100-200 years ago. During the month of Śravaṇa (July-August), annual worship is held here.
